api_key.description: Bearer token. If omitted, the LOGFIRE_API_KEY environment variable is used.

base_url.description: Base URL for the Logfire API. If omitted, the provider uses LOGFIRE_BASE_URL or infers the SaaS endpoint from the api_key region. Self-hosted customers should set this explicitly.

custom_headers.description: Additional HTTP headers to include on every Logfire API request. Intended for proxy, gateway, or edge authentication. Provider-managed headers cannot be overridden.

organization.description: Name of the organization that resources act in. Self-hosted instances only. The provider exchanges the instance-admin `api_key` for a short-lived token for this organization. If omitted, the provider uses LOGFIRE_ORGANIZATION. If neither is set, resources act in the organization of the `api_key`. The `organization` argument of `logfire_project` overrides this value.

block.description: Configure the Logfire API endpoint and credentials used by all resources.

active.description: Whether the alert is active (defaults to true on creation).

schedule_id.description: ID of a `logfire_schedule`. The channel is notified only inside the schedule's windows. Omit it to notify the channel at all times.

channel_assignments.description: Channels to notify, each with an optional delivery schedule. Set it to `[]` to notify no channel. This is the same type as `alerts.<tier>.channel_assignments` on `logfire_slo`, so one value (for example a `locals` entry) can configure both.

environments.description: Deployment environments to scope the query to. Empty = all environments (no filter).

frequency.description: Evaluation frequency, as a duration from `1m` to `24h` (for example `5m`, `20m`, `1h`). Equivalent spellings are accepted and kept as written.

identity_columns.description: Result columns whose values identify an occurrence. One to 8 unique names of 1 to 128 characters.

missing_behavior.description: The close reason of an occurrence that is missing for `missing_runs` runs. One of `no_longer_matching` or `expire`.

missing_runs.description: Consecutive runs without the occurrence, 1 to 100, before it closes.

pending_runs.description: Consecutive matching runs, 1 to 100, before a new occurrence fires.

instance_policy.description: Track each result row as its own occurrence, keyed by the identity columns, instead of evaluating the whole result as one. Needs an organization with alert instance policies enabled, otherwise the API answers 403 `alert_instances_not_enabled`. Remove the attribute to evaluate the whole result as one again. The API's deprecated `continuity_runs` is not exposed. A new policy gets the value of `missing_runs`, and a change keeps the stored value unless it is lower than `missing_runs`.

notify_when.description: Notification rule. Must match API enum. `instances_changed` needs `instance_policy`. It sends one notification for each run that opens or closes occurrences, listing them, from Logfire v2026-11-13.01.

project_id.description: Project ID (UUID) used for alert API paths.

query.description: SQL / query string used by the alert.

time_window.description: Lookback window, as a duration from `1m` to `30d` (for example `20m`, `1h30m`, `7d`). The API caps this relative to `frequency` - a longer window requires a less frequent evaluation - and reports that itself. Equivalent spellings are accepted and kept as written.

watermark.description: Provider-managed watermark (lateness tolerance) sent to the API.

block.description: Manages a Logfire alert.

active.description: False once the key is disabled. Disable/enable is managed outside Terraform; deleting the resource revokes the key.

all_projects.description: True for org-wide keys with no project scope.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the key was created.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user that created the key, when known.

description.description: Free-form description. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp (for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`). If omitted, the key does not expire. Changing it replaces the key: expiry cannot be updated in place (an expired key cannot be re-enabled; create a new key instead).

cache_enabled.description: Whether gateway responses are cached. Null inherits the project default.

spending_limit_daily.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per day. Null means no limit.

spending_limit_monthly.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per month. Null means no limit.

spending_limit_total.description: Maximum lifetime gateway spend in whole US dollars. Null means no limit.

spending_limit_weekly.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per week. Null means no limit.

gateway.description: Gateway per-scope settings for keys with the `project:gateway_proxy` scope. Updatable in place. Removing the block clears every cap the key carries.

id.description: API key identifier. Use this identifier to import an existing key.

name.description: Display name for the key. Can be updated in place.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the key is scoped to. Omit for an org-wide key. Changing the project replaces the key. Scopes `project:read_otlp`, `project:write_otlp`, and `project:gateway_proxy` require a project.

project_name.description: Name of the project the key is scoped to, if any.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes granted to the key (for example `project:write_otlp`). Changing scopes replaces the key: scopes cannot be updated in place.

token.description: The plaintext API key. Only returned on creation; never returned again by the API.

block.description: Manages a Logfire API key. Write tokens (`project:write_otlp`), read tokens (`project:read_otlp`), gateway keys (`project:gateway_proxy`), and management keys are all API keys with different scopes. The new key can never exceed the provider credential's own grant: its scopes must be a subset of the provider `api_key` scopes, so the provider key needs `organization:create_api_key` plus every scope it delegates.

base_url.description: Opsgenie API base URL, for example `https://api.eu.opsgenie.com` for an EU account. Only for `opsgenie` channels. Omitting it on an existing channel retains the current value; set it to `https://api.opsgenie.com` explicitly to return to the default US endpoint.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID (for example `C0123456789`) the notifications are posted to. The Logfire Slack bot must already be a member of the channel.

include_agent_prompt.description: Whether Slack issue notifications include the "Ask your agent" MCP prompt line. Defaults to `true` for new Slack channels. Omitting it on an existing channel retains the current setting; set it to `true` explicitly to re-enable the prompt.

install_id.description: ID of the organization's Slack App or PagerDuty App installation, created by connecting the platform in the Logfire UI (Organization Settings -> Connections). The installation must belong to the same organization, be active, and match the channel type.

recipients.description: Email addresses the channel notifies, 1 to 50. Required for `email` channels, which need a Logfire plan with custom email recipients. Logfire normalizes each address, for example by lowercasing its domain. The provider keeps the configured spelling when Logfire stores an equivalent one. A recipient who unsubscribes leaves the channel, and Logfire rejects an update that adds them back until you remove the address from the configuration.

region.description: PagerDuty account region (`us` or `eu`). When omitted, Logfire uses the US Events API endpoint. Only for `pagerduty` channels; a `pagerduty-integration` channel takes its region from the connected account.

routing_key.description: PagerDuty Events API v2 integration routing key. Only for `pagerduty` channels; `pagerduty-integration` channels resolve the key from the installation instead.

service_id.description: Logfire's ID (a UUID) for the PagerDuty service incidents are opened on, as approved for the installation when connecting PagerDuty. This is not PagerDuty's own service ID. Required for `pagerduty-integration` channels.

block.description: Required channel configuration.
Manages a Logfire alert channel. Import accepts the channel UUID or its name (label).

id.description: Dashboard UUID assigned by the backend.

managed_allow_edits.description: Whether the Logfire UI and the Logfire MCP server can edit the dashboard. Defaults to `false` for a new dashboard. A Logfire instance without managed dashboards, or with them turned off, ignores a configured value. Terraform then warns and plans the value again on every run until Logfire applies it. A dashboard created by an earlier provider version stays editable until you set the attribute. Removing the attribute keeps the current value. Set it to `true` to allow edits again.

project_id.description: Project UUID used for API paths.

block.description:
Manages a Logfire dashboard.

The provider marks the dashboard as managed by the tool that applies it, and Logfire shows a Managed badge on it. A new dashboard is also locked against edits in the Logfire UI and through the Logfire MCP server unless `managed_allow_edits` is `true`. The lock does not cover the dashboards API, which the provider uses. A Logfire instance without managed dashboards ignores the marker. An existing dashboard gets the marker on its next update.

adopt_existing_service_name.description: Allow creation when telemetry already reports under `name`. Set this before replacing `service_namespace` or `environment` without changing `name`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the application was created.

environment.description: Immutable value used to overwrite `deployment.environment.name` when set.

name.description: Application name. Logfire overwrites `service.name` with this value. The API cannot rename an application, so changing this replaces it, unless the new value is its current name in Logfire. After a rename in the Logfire UI, Terraform keeps the configured name and plans no change. Update this value to the new name to follow the rename without a replacement.

project_id.description: UUID of the project that owns the application.

service_namespace.description: Immutable value used to overwrite `service.namespace` when set.

token.description: An active restricted browser token. The provider recovers this value on refresh and import.

token_id.description: Identifier of an active restricted browser token.

block.description: Experimental: the backing management API is currently enabled only in Logfire staging environments. Manages an immutable Logfire frontend application identity and exposes one active restricted browser token. Use `logfire_frontend_application_token` for two-phase rotation. Creation is not retried automatically because the operation is not idempotent; after an uncertain failure, list the applications and import the matching identity instead of applying again.

adopt_token_id.description: Existing active token to adopt instead of issuing another. Use the application's `token_id` for the initial handoff, then remove this resource only after a separately managed replacement has been deployed.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the token was created.

last_used_at.description: Timestamp when the token was last used, when known.

project_id.description: UUID of the project that owns the application.

revoke_on_destroy.description: Revoke this token when its resource is destroyed. Before destroying the entire application tree, set this to `false` in a separate apply for the last token so application deletion can revoke all attached tokens.

status.description: Token status. A managed token remains in state only while active.

token.description: Active restricted browser token. The provider recovers this value on refresh and import.

block.description: Experimental: the backing management API is currently enabled only in Logfire staging environments. Manages one active token for a Logfire frontend application. Rotate in two applies with two resource blocks: add the replacement and deploy its `token`, then remove the old resource to revoke it. The provider never revokes an old token while creating a new one. Token issuance is not retried automatically because the operation is not idempotent; after an uncertain failure, list the application's tokens and adopt the one unambiguous new active token. Before destroying the whole application tree, set the last token's `revoke_on_destroy` to `false` in a separate apply; application deletion then revokes every attached token.

active.description: False once the key is disabled. Disable/enable is managed outside Terraform; deleting the resource revokes the key.

cache_enabled.description: Whether gateway responses are cached. Null inherits the project default. Can be updated in place; setting it to null restores the default.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the key was created.

description.description: Free-form description. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp (for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`). If omitted, the key does not expire. Changing it replaces the key.

id.description: Gateway API key identifier. Use this identifier to import an existing key.

name.description: Display name for the key. Can be updated in place.

project_id.description: UUID of the project the key proxies for. Gateway keys always require a project. Changing it replaces the key.

project_name.description: Name of the project the key proxies for.

spending_limit_daily.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per day. Null means no limit. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

spending_limit_monthly.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per month. Null means no limit. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

spending_limit_total.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per lifetime. Null means no limit. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

spending_limit_weekly.description: Maximum gateway spend in whole US dollars per week. Null means no limit. Can be updated in place; setting it to null clears it.

token.description: The plaintext gateway API key. Only returned on creation; never returned again by the API.

block.description: Manages a project-scoped AI Gateway API key (`project:gateway_proxy` scope). Do not confuse this with `logfire_gateway_provider`, which configures an upstream LLM provider credential. The provider credential needs `organization:create_api_key` plus `project:gateway_proxy` delegation; a project-scoped operator key for this is minted from the organization-level API keys page with the project selected.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the endpoint was created.

active.description: Whether the Gateway routes to this provider. Defaults to true.

priority.description: The Gateway tries providers with a higher priority first. Providers with the same priority are tried in a random order that follows their weights. Defaults to 0.

provider_id.description: UUID of a `logfire_gateway_provider` in the same organization.

weight.description: Positive relative weight among providers with the same priority. Defaults to 1.

providers.description: Complete set of providers the endpoint routes to. A change replaces the whole set in one request. At least one provider must be active.

slug.description: Organization-unique endpoint slug. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

block.description: Manages an organization-owned AI Gateway endpoint and the providers it routes to. Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read_gateway and organization:write_gateway scopes (organization:read and organization:write are also accepted). Endpoints that use built-in providers or more than 100 providers are not supported. Import accepts the endpoint UUID or its organization-unique slug.

daily_usd.description: The daily limit in whole US dollars. A day starts at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no daily limit.

monthly_usd.description: The monthly limit in whole US dollars. A month starts on the 1st at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no monthly limit.

project_id.description: The UUID of the project that the limits apply to. Changing it replaces the resource.

weekly_usd.description: The weekly limit in whole US dollars. A week starts on Monday at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no weekly limit.

block.description: Manages the AI Gateway spending limits of one project. When the project goes over a limit, the Gateway blocks every credential in the project until the window resets. Requires a plan that includes the AI Gateway and a token with `organization:read_gateway` and `organization:write_gateway` scopes (`organization:read` and `organization:write` are also accepted).

api_key.description: Upstream API key. For google-vertex, the service account key JSON. Changing it rotates the credential in place. Logfire never returns this value; Terraform retains it in state. External credential changes cannot be detected. After import, the next apply sets the configured key.

bedrock_api.description: Bedrock API variant: runtime or mantle. Required only for bedrock; can be updated in place.

bedrock_region.description: AWS region used to derive the Bedrock endpoint, for example us-east-1. Required only for bedrock; can be updated in place.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the provider was created.

endpoint.description: Upstream endpoint URL, for example https://my-resource.openai.azure.com or https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com. Required only for azure and google-vertex; can be updated in place.

id.description: Provider UUID. Use this identifier to import an existing provider.

require_pricing.description: Require known model pricing before forwarding requests. Defaults to true.

slug.description: Organization-unique provider slug. Changing it replaces the provider.

vendor.description: Upstream vendor: openai, anthropic, azure, bedrock, doubleword, google-vertex, groq, huggingface, or mistral. Changing it replaces the provider.

block.description: Manages an organization-owned AI Gateway provider. Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read and organization:write scopes. Built-in providers and arbitrary upstream URLs are not supported. Import accepts the provider UUID or its organization-unique slug.

daily_usd.description: The daily limit in whole US dollars. A day starts at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no daily limit.

monthly_usd.description: The monthly limit in whole US dollars. A month starts on the 1st at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no monthly limit.

weekly_usd.description: The weekly limit in whole US dollars. A week starts on Monday at 00:00 UTC. Omit it to have no weekly limit.

block.description: Manages the AI Gateway spending limits of the organization. An organization limit caps the Gateway spend of every project and credential in the organization. Requires a plan that includes the AI Gateway and a token with `organization:read_gateway` and `organization:write_gateway` scopes (`organization:read` and `organization:write` are also accepted).

api_mapping_status.description: `active` when sign-in uses the stored mapping. `overridden_by_environment` when the Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping` is set, which makes the stored mapping unused.

group_id.description: The identity-provider group ID. Each group ID appears once.

organization.description: The organization name. The organization must exist.

project.description: The project name. The project must exist in the organization.

role.description: The built-in or custom project role name. The API does not check it, so a wrong name gives no error and sign-in skips the role.

project_roles.description: The roles that members of the group get in projects of this organization. Only listed projects are managed. Omit it or use an empty list for none.

role.description: The built-in or custom organization role name. The API does not check it, so a wrong name gives no error and sign-in skips the role.

organization_roles.description: The roles that members of the group get in organizations.

mapping.description: The complete mapping, in the order that the instance stores it. An empty list stores no mapping.

block.description: Manages the identity-provider group mapping of a self-hosted Logfire instance. The mapping assigns organization and project roles to the members of identity-provider groups at their next sign-in. The instance has one mapping, so declare this resource once. It conflicts with the Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping`, which overrides the mapping that the API stores. The provider credential must be an API key from the admin organization with the `instance:admin` scope (`organization:admin` is equivalent).

billing_email.description: Logfire no longer stores a billing email for an organization. The provider does not send this value to Logfire and keeps the configured value only in state. It will be removed in v0.4.0.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the organization was created.

deletion_protection.description: Prevents accidental destroy when true (defaults to true). Set to false and apply before deleting this resource.

display_name.description: Display name shown in the UI.

has_admin_panel.description: Whether the organization has access to the admin panel.

id.description: Organization UUID assigned by the backend.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the organization was last updated.

block.description: Manages a Logfire organization. This resource is only available for self-hosted deployments and requires an API key created in the admin organization (the one with the admin panel) carrying the `organization:admin` scope. A key minted inside another organization cannot manage organizations regardless of its scopes. Reading, updating, and deleting an organization authenticates with a short-lived organization-scoped token exchanged from that key, so every operation beyond creating and listing requires a Logfire backend from 2026-06-25 (v2026-06-25.01) or newer; creating and listing organizations require 2026-06-03 (v2026-06-03.01) or newer.

id.description: Opaque backend project ID (not the slug).

name.description: Project name/slug. Must be unique within the organization.

organization.description: Organization name. Defaults to the provider `organization`, else the organization of the provider credential. Setting it acts in that organization through the instance-admin token exchange (self-hosted only). Changing it replaces the project when the new name is another existing organization than `organization_id`. Logfire cannot move a project between organizations, so a replacement deletes the project with all its data and creates an empty project. Set `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to block it. A new name for the same organization, a name that is not known yet, or a name the instance does not list yet updates in place. After an organization is renamed, a refresh updates this value.

organization_id.description: ID of the organization that the project is in. Set when the project is in a named organization, through the `organization` argument or the provider `organization`. Null for a project in the organization of the credential.

block.description: Manages a Logfire project. By default the credential creates the project in its own organization and must hold `organization:create_project`. On a self-hosted instance, an instance-admin credential creates the project in another organization with the `organization` argument or the provider `organization`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the token was created.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user that created the token.

description.description: Description is fixed to "Created by Public API" for provider-managed tokens.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp for the token (for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`). If omitted, the token does not expire.

project_id.description: UUID of the project that owns the token.

project_name.description: Name of the project that owns the token.

token.description: The generated read token. Only returned on creation.

token_prefix.description: Prefix of the generated read token.

block.description: Manages a Logfire read token. Equivalent to logfire_api_key with scopes `["project:read_otlp"]`. Creating it requires the `project:read_token` scope on a credential that can reach the project. Import is not supported: the API returns the token value only at creation, so an imported token could never reproduce its secret in state. Recreate a token with Terraform to adopt it.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the windows, for example `Europe/London`.

days.description: ISO weekday numbers: `1` is Monday and `7` is Sunday.

end_time.description: End of the window, as 24-hour `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` in `timezone`. A read keeps your spelling when it denotes the same time, and shows seconds only when they are not zero.

start_time.description: Start of the window, as 24-hour `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` in `timezone`. A read keeps your spelling when it denotes the same time, and shows seconds only when they are not zero.

windows.description: Time windows in which the schedule delivers. At least one.

block.description: Manages an organization-level Logfire delivery schedule. A channel assignment with a `schedule_id` notifies its channel only inside the schedule's windows. Use it in `channel_assignments` on `logfire_alert` and in `alerts.<tier>.channel_assignments` on `logfire_slo`. Deleting a schedule makes the channel assignments that use it notify at all times. The provider credential needs `organization:read_channel` and `organization:write_channel`. The schedules API needs Logfire v2026-09-23.01 or newer.

alert_id.description: ID of the tier's alert. Null only for an SLO created before Logfire kept all three tier alerts, when the tier could not fire at the SLO's target. The provider then plans an update of the SLO, even when no attribute changed, and that update creates the missing alert.

schedule_id.description: ID of a `logfire_schedule`. The channel is notified only inside the schedule's windows. Omit it to notify the channel at all times.

channel_assignments.description: Channels of this tier's alert, each with an optional delivery schedule. The provider writes the value to the alert on create, and on update when it differs from what the alert has. It is read back from the alert, so a change made on the Logfire alerts page shows as drift. Set it to `[]` to remove every channel. It is the same type as `logfire_alert.channel_assignments`.

severity.description: `page` for the `fast` and `medium` tiers, `ticket` for the `slow` tier.

viable.description: False when the tier cannot fire at the SLO's `target_percent`. The alert keeps its channels but is not evaluated until a target change makes the tier viable.

fast.description: The `fast` burn-rate tier's alert (severity `page`). Omit it to leave that alert's channels as they are.

alert_id.description: ID of the tier's alert. Null only for an SLO created before Logfire kept all three tier alerts, when the tier could not fire at the SLO's target. The provider then plans an update of the SLO, even when no attribute changed, and that update creates the missing alert.

schedule_id.description: ID of a `logfire_schedule`. The channel is notified only inside the schedule's windows. Omit it to notify the channel at all times.

channel_assignments.description: Channels of this tier's alert, each with an optional delivery schedule. The provider writes the value to the alert on create, and on update when it differs from what the alert has. It is read back from the alert, so a change made on the Logfire alerts page shows as drift. Set it to `[]` to remove every channel. It is the same type as `logfire_alert.channel_assignments`.

severity.description: `page` for the `fast` and `medium` tiers, `ticket` for the `slow` tier.

viable.description: False when the tier cannot fire at the SLO's `target_percent`. The alert keeps its channels but is not evaluated until a target change makes the tier viable.

medium.description: The `medium` burn-rate tier's alert (severity `page`). Omit it to leave that alert's channels as they are.

alert_id.description: ID of the tier's alert. Null only for an SLO created before Logfire kept all three tier alerts, when the tier could not fire at the SLO's target. The provider then plans an update of the SLO, even when no attribute changed, and that update creates the missing alert.

schedule_id.description: ID of a `logfire_schedule`. The channel is notified only inside the schedule's windows. Omit it to notify the channel at all times.

channel_assignments.description: Channels of this tier's alert, each with an optional delivery schedule. The provider writes the value to the alert on create, and on update when it differs from what the alert has. It is read back from the alert, so a change made on the Logfire alerts page shows as drift. Set it to `[]` to remove every channel. It is the same type as `logfire_alert.channel_assignments`.

severity.description: `page` for the `fast` and `medium` tiers, `ticket` for the `slow` tier.

viable.description: False when the tier cannot fire at the SLO's `target_percent`. The alert keeps its channels but is not evaluated until a target change makes the tier viable.

slow.description: The `slow` burn-rate tier's alert (severity `ticket`). Omit it to leave that alert's channels as they are.

alerts.description: The SLO's burn-rate alerts, one per tier: `fast` and `medium` (severity `page`) and `slow` (severity `ticket`). Each alert exists as long as the SLO does. Configure `channel_assignments` on the tiers whose delivery Terraform should manage. A tier that is not configured is not sent and not managed: the provider reports its current channels and never changes them. Setting `channel_assignments` needs Logfire v2026-09-23.01 or newer. An older release does not apply them, so the provider fails the apply with an error. `alerts` is null when the Logfire release does not return the SLO's alerts.

bad_query.description: SQL boolean expression selecting the bad events counted by the SLO. Required for every mode except `metric_aggregation = "histogram_threshold"`, which uses `threshold` and `comparison` instead.

comparison.description: For `metric_aggregation = "histogram_threshold"`: the good side of the `threshold`. `less_than` (good is below the threshold, the latency case) or `greater_than`. Required for that mode, and must be omitted otherwise.

environments.description: Deployment environments the SLO is scoped to. Omit to cover all environments.

metric_aggregation.description: How a `metrics` SLO aggregates its SLI: `additive` (sum of scalar values, for delta-count metrics), `gauge_fraction` (fraction of samples meeting the condition, for gauges), `counter_rate` (sum of per-series increases, for cumulative counters), or `histogram_threshold` (fraction of histogram observations past a threshold; uses `threshold` and `comparison` instead of `bad_query`, and requires `source = "metrics"`). Ignored when `source = "records"`. Defaults to `additive`.

project_id.description: Project ID (UUID) used for SLO API paths.

rolling_window.description: Rolling evaluation window as a duration string (e.g. `"24h"`, `"30d"`). Must be between 1h and 90d. The API enforces a lower effective cap: the window cannot exceed your subscription plan's maximum SLO window, nor the project's data retention for the SLO source (`records` or `metrics`) — a longer window would compute against missing data. Requests over either cap are rejected with a validation error.

scope_kind.description: What the SLO is anchored to: a service (`service`) or an LLM provider (`provider`). Defaults to `service`. Changing it forces a new SLO.

scope_value.description: The service name (`scope_kind = "service"`) or provider slug like `openai` (`scope_kind = "provider"`). Changing it forces a new SLO.

source.description: Whether the SLO ratio is computed over span events (`records`) or metric values (`metrics`). Defaults to `records`.

target_percent.description: Target percentage as a decimal string, exclusively between 0 and 100 (e.g. `"99.9"`).

threshold.description: For `metric_aggregation = "histogram_threshold"`: the cutoff in the metric's native unit, as a decimal string (e.g. `"60000"` on a `_ms` latency metric). Required for that mode, and must be omitted otherwise.

total_query.description: SQL boolean expression selecting all events counted by the SLO.

block.description:
Manages a Logfire SLO (Service Level Objective).

~> **Experimental:** this resource is backed by a Logfire API that is not yet stable. Its schema and behavior may change in backwards-incompatible ways in future releases. SLOs also require a Logfire plan that includes them.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the token was created.

created_by_name.description: Display name of the user that created the token.

description.description: Description is fixed to "Created by Public API" for provider-managed tokens.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC3339 expiration timestamp for the token (for example `2026-12-31T23:59:59Z`). If omitted, the token does not expire.

project_id.description: UUID of the project that owns the token.

project_name.description: Name of the project that owns the token.

token.description: The generated write token. Only returned on creation.

token_prefix.description: Prefix of the generated write token.

block.description: Manages a Logfire write token. Equivalent to logfire_api_key with scopes `["project:write_otlp"]`. Creating it requires the `project:write_token` scope on a credential that can reach the project. Import is not supported: the API returns the token value only at creation, so an imported token could never reproduce its secret in state. Recreate a token with Terraform to adopt it.

account_subdomain.description: PagerDuty account subdomain, such as `acme` from `acme.pagerduty.com`.

region.description: PagerDuty account region (`us` or `eu`). Defaults to `us`.

block.description: Resolves a PagerDuty service approved through a Logfire connection to the IDs required by a `pagerduty-integration` channel. PagerDuty's external service ID is resolved to Logfire's internal installation and resource IDs. The provider API key requires the `organization:read_channel` scope.
